summary: Final readout for Selverant Therapeutics Inc integrating HepG2 viability context and the Mammalian-cell micronucleus assessment. It records the lower-exposure repeat request and distinguishes the investigation narrative from trends supported by the supplied aggregate table.

slides.title: ST03: viability and micronucleus follow-up
slides.subtitle:
OT-15-S0064 | Selverant Therapeutics Inc | 07/14/2015
Dr N. Takamori | Osterquill Toxicology Inc

slides.title: Repeat at lower exposure before attribution
bullets: {{PRJ0119:n_compounds}} test articles in the HepG2 viability screen.
Selverant Therapeutics Inc requested a lower-exposure repeat before attributing the micronucleus signal to genotoxicity.
The supplied aggregate table does not demonstrate a consistent concentration-related micronucleus increase.

slides.title: Exposure context and control-validity limits
bullets: HepG2 ATP-content endpoints at 24 h and 48 h provide viability context, not TK6 exposure measurements.
TK6 exposures: 3 h with and without S9; 24 h without S9.
Positive-control values and formal acceptance determinations are absent from this summary; consult original observation sheets before regulatory use.
No live-animal procedures are described in this package.

slides.title: Mammalian-cell micronucleus assessment: exposure and RPD
Interpretation at the client discussion
bullets: RPD declines at the highest concentration in the S9-activated short exposure, qualifying the exposure interpretation.
Micronucleus frequencies vary around corresponding vehicles without a consistent dose-related increase.
The investigation narrative associates the concern with cytotoxic exposure; these aggregate rows alone do not establish that association.
Do not infer a definitive genotoxicity conclusion from this subset.
slides.notes: Kenji Morita should reconcile individual scoring and control-validity observations before the repeat is interpreted. HepG2 and TK6 responses are not interchangeable.

slides.title: Lower-exposure repeat: decision and deliverables
bullets: Retain matched vehicle and positive controls under each exposure schedule.
Use closer concentration spacing below the cytotoxic region; report proliferation alongside micronucleus scoring.
Link test article identity, S9 status, exposure and scoring observations under {{PRJ0119:lims_id}}.
Dr N. Takamori will interpret the repeat with Kenji Morita; Lucia Moretti will review traceability and compliance scope.
The repeat is the next decision point, not an established resolution of the concern.
